title: One DynamoDB write: router, partition leader, and a quorum of replicas
captions: Your request first reaches a request router. It checks who you are, then looks up which partition holds this key. That map comes from the metadata service and is cached.
Each partition is a small group of replicas in different Availability Zones. The router sends the write to the group's leader.
The leader writes a log record and sends it to its peers. The group uses Multi-Paxos to agree on a leader and on each write.
Once a quorum, two of the three replicas, has saved the record, the write is acknowledged. One slow zone does not block it.
A strongly consistent read must go to the leader. An eventually consistent read can go to any replica, so it can be a little behind. It also costs half as much.
